8	# CONTRACT-004: Harness Implementation Contract
9	
10	| Field | Value |
11	|-------|-------|
12	| Status | Draft |
13	| Date | 2026-05-14 |
14	| Scope | Internal interface every Fizeau harness package implements; service-side consumers depend only on this contract, never on harness-specific exports. |
15	| Companion | CONTRACT-003 (service-facing API); ADR-014 (decision rationale) |
16	
17	## Purpose
18	
19	CONTRACT-003 specifies the public Fizeau service surface. It does not specify
20	the internal contract that each harness implementation
21	(`internal/harnesses/<name>/`) satisfies. Today that internal contract is the
22	3-method `harnesses.Harness` interface plus an ad-hoc collection of
23	per-harness exported symbols (~80 of them across claude, codex, gemini)
24	that the service imports directly: `ClaudeQuotaSnapshot`,
25	`ReadClaudeQuota`, `DecideClaudeQuotaRouting`, `CodexAuthPath`,
26	`ReadAuthEvidence`, `ResolveClaudeFamilyAlias`, and so on.
27	
28	This contract closes that gap. It defines the complete normative interface
29	every harness implementation MUST satisfy and constrains the service to
30	consume only that interface. Per-harness symbol leakage is the failure
31	mode CONTRACT-004 exists to prevent.
32	
33	## Scope
34	
35	In scope:
36	
37	- The Go interface set every `internal/harnesses/<name>/` package
38	  implements.
39	- The universal types those interfaces return.
40	- Cache and refresh ownership.
41	- Conformance evidence requirements.
42	- Projection rules from internal harness types to the CONTRACT-003
43	  public types (`QuotaState`, `AccountStatus`, `HarnessInfo`,
44	  `ProviderInfo`).
45	
46	Out of scope:
47	
48	- The CLI/network behavior of any specific harness binary (covered by
49	  primary-harness-capability-baseline.md and per-harness specs).
50	- The cassette/replay transport contract (ADR-002).
51	- The public service contract (CONTRACT-003).
52	
53	## Interface Set
54	
55	Every harness implementation MUST implement `Harness`. It MAY additionally
56	implement any of `QuotaHarness`, `AccountHarness`, and
57	`ModelDiscoveryHarness`. The service uses Go interface assertions to
58	discover which optional contracts a harness satisfies and consumes them
59	through the interface only.
60	
61	```go
62	package harnesses
63	
64	// Harness is the minimum every harness implements.
65	type Harness interface {
66	    // Info returns identity + capability metadata. Stable across the
67	    // process lifetime; cheap to call from request hot paths.
68	    Info() HarnessInfo
69	
70	    // HealthCheck triggers a fresh, lightweight readiness probe (binary
71	    // present and executable; non-blocking auth state read where
72	    // possible). Returns nil when ready. MUST NOT drive interactive
73	    // sessions or block on network.
74	    HealthCheck(ctx context.Context) error
75	
76	    // Execute runs one resolved request and returns an event channel.
77	    // The channel emits zero or more progress/text/tool events followed
78	    // by exactly one EventTypeFinal event, then closes. Setup failures
79	    // (binary missing, PTY allocation failure) return as the second
80	    // return value; per-run failures (auth, quota, parser desync,
81	    // timeout, cancellation) MUST be reported via the final event with
82	    // Status != "success".
83	    Execute(ctx context.Context, req ExecuteRequest) (<-chan Event, error)
84	}
85	
86	// QuotaHarness is implemented by harnesses that own a subscription or
87	// quota window. claude, codex, gemini implement; opencode, pi do not.
88	type QuotaHarness interface {
89	    Harness
90	
91	    // QuotaStatus returns the current quota state from the harness's
92	    // owned cache, with Fresh/Age computed against `now`. MUST be cheap
93	    // (no live probe) and safe to call on every routing decision.
94	    // Absence of evidence is reported via State=QuotaUnavailable on a
95	    // valid QuotaStatus value; the error return is reserved for call
96	    // failure (ctx cancelled, IO failure, lock acquisition failure).
97	    QuotaStatus(ctx context.Context, now time.Time) (QuotaStatus, error)
98	
99	    // RefreshQuota drives the harness's live probe (PTY, CLI, or other
100	    // owned transport), persists the result through the harness's owned
101	    // cache, and returns the resulting status. RefreshQuota probes
102	    // unconditionally on every successful lock acquisition; it does
103	    // NOT skip the probe based on cache freshness. Cache-freshness
104	    // deduplication is the caller's responsibility: callers that want
105	    // a possibly-stale-but-cheap read use QuotaStatus; callers that
106	    // orchestrate refresh cadence (e.g. a periodic scheduler) skip
107	    // ticks when the last-known CapturedAt is within QuotaFreshness()
108	    // of the current time. Callers that want a fresh probe call
109	    // RefreshQuota and accept the probe cost.
110	    //
111	    // RefreshQuota is single-flight per harness instance: concurrent
112	    // callers block on the harness's cache lock (per ADR-012). Queued
113	    // callers MUST NOT initiate a second probe — once the in-flight
114	    // refresh completes and releases the lock, queued callers read the
115	    // just-written cached state and return it. The contract guarantee
116	    // is "one probe per single-flight cohort," not "one probe per
117	    // call." Probe failure is reported as a QuotaStatus with
118	    // State=QuotaUnavailable (or QuotaUnauthenticated when the probe
119	    // identifies the failure as auth-related), not as an error. The
120	    // error return is reserved for call failure: ctx cancelled before
121	    // lock acquisition, lock acquisition timeout under deadline,
122	    // unrecoverable lock-file corruption, or unrecoverable IO failure.
123	    // Lock contention itself is not a failure — the caller waits.
124	    RefreshQuota(ctx context.Context) (QuotaStatus, error)
125	
126	    // QuotaFreshness returns the harness's freshness window (e.g. 15m).
127	    // Service code uses this for stale-cache scheduling. Constant for
128	    // the harness; cheap to call.
129	    QuotaFreshness() time.Duration
130	
131	    // SupportedLimitIDs returns the harness's stable set of emitted
132	    // Windows[].LimitID values (e.g. "session", "weekly-all",
133	    // "weekly-sonnet" for claude; "tier-flash", "tier-pro" for
134	    // gemini). Constant for the harness; the harness's package doc
135	    // also enumerates this set for human readers. The conformance
136	    // suite reads this value to verify that emitted Windows[].LimitID
137	    // strings are a subset of the documented set, and that the set
138	    // does not regress between binary versions without a deprecation
139	    // cycle. Empty slice is allowed for harnesses that emit no
140	    // windows.
141	    SupportedLimitIDs() []string
142	}
143	
144	// AccountHarness is implemented by harnesses that expose authentication
145	// or account state independent of quota. gemini implements this so its
146	// AuthSnapshot can refresh on its own cadence (7-day freshness window vs.
147	// quota's 15-minute window). claude and codex embed account in their
148	// quota probe and MAY satisfy AccountHarness by re-projecting from
149	// QuotaStatus.Account; that is allowed but not required.
150	type AccountHarness interface {
151	    Harness
152	
153	    // AccountStatus returns the harness's current account/auth state.
154	    // Cheap; reads cached evidence only. Absence of evidence is
155	    // reported via AccountSnapshot.Authenticated=false and
156	    // .Unauthenticated=false (i.e. unknown) on a valid snapshot; the
157	    // error return is reserved for call failure.
158	    AccountStatus(ctx context.Context, now time.Time) (AccountSnapshot, error)
159	
160	    // RefreshAccount drives the harness's account probe (file read,
161	    // CLI call, OAuth state lookup) and persists the result.
162	    // Single-flight per harness instance via the harness's account
163	    // cache lock; concurrent callers block. Probe failure is reported
164	    // via AccountSnapshot fields, not as an error.
165	    RefreshAccount(ctx context.Context) (AccountSnapshot, error)
166	
167	    // AccountFreshness returns the harness's account freshness window
168	    // (e.g. 7 days for gemini, 15 minutes for harnesses whose account
169	    // refreshes coupled with quota). Constant for the harness; cheap.
170	    // Used by the service refresh scheduler to decide when account
171	    // state is stale independent of quota state.
172	    AccountFreshness() time.Duration
173	}
174	
175	// ModelDiscoveryHarness is implemented by harnesses whose model surface
176	// extends beyond a single Info().DefaultModel — i.e. they support family
177	// aliases (sonnet, gpt, gemini) that resolve through discovery evidence.
178	// All five harnesses implement this in the current registry.
179	type ModelDiscoveryHarness interface {
180	    Harness
181	
182	    // DefaultModelSnapshot returns the harness's seed/fallback discovery
183	    // snapshot. Used to bootstrap the catalog before the first live
184	    // refresh lands. Stable for the harness; cheap.
185	    DefaultModelSnapshot() ModelDiscoverySnapshot
186	
187	    // ResolveModelAlias maps a family-style requested model (e.g.
188	    // "sonnet", "gpt", "gemini") to a concrete model ID using the
189	    // provided discovery snapshot. Returns ErrAliasNotResolvable if the
190	    // family is not recognized or the snapshot has no matching concrete
191	    // model.
192	    ResolveModelAlias(family string, snapshot ModelDiscoverySnapshot) (string, error)
193	
194	    // SupportedAliases returns the harness's stable set of family
195	    // aliases ResolveModelAlias recognizes (e.g. "sonnet", "opus",
196	    // "haiku" for claude). Constant for the harness; the harness's
197	    // package doc also enumerates this set for human readers. The
198	    // conformance suite uses this value to verify ResolveModelAlias
199	    // covers each documented family (positive path) and rejects
200	    // out-of-set families with ErrAliasNotResolvable (negative path).
201	    // Empty slice is allowed for harnesses that recognize no family
202	    // aliases (e.g. opencode, pi).
203	    SupportedAliases() []string
204	}
205	```

325	## Cache and Refresh Ownership
326	
327	Each `QuotaHarness` and `AccountHarness` implementation owns:
328	
329	- The on-disk cache path (defaulted to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/<harness>/quota.json`
330	  or `$XDG_STATE_HOME/<harness>/account.json`; harness-specific paths are
331	  acceptable when documented).
332	- The cache schema, including version bumps and migration.
333	- The freshness window returned by `QuotaFreshness()`.
334	- The probe transport (PTY, CLI, file read).
335	- Lock coordination per ADR-012 (per-source on-disk cache).
336	
337	Service-side code MUST NOT read, write, or compute paths for these caches
338	directly. Operator-visible cache paths SHOULD be exposed through a single
339	service-level diagnostic surface (e.g. `Service.DiagnosticPaths()`) that
340	calls back into each harness via a documented method, rather than the
341	service importing per-harness path functions.
342	
343	## Projection to CONTRACT-003
344	
345	The service layer projects harness-level types onto CONTRACT-003 public
346	types as follows. The projection is the only place service code converts
347	between layers; nothing else in the service may read fields off
348	`QuotaStatus` and re-emit them under different names.
349	
350	| CONTRACT-003 public field | CONTRACT-004 source |
351	|---------------------------|---------------------|
352	| `service.QuotaState.Windows` | `QuotaStatus.Windows` |
353	| `service.QuotaState.CapturedAt` | `QuotaStatus.CapturedAt` |
354	| `service.QuotaState.Fresh` | `QuotaStatus.Fresh` |
355	| `service.QuotaState.Source` | `QuotaStatus.Source` |
356	| `service.QuotaState.Status` | `QuotaStatus.State` (string-cast); when `QuotaStatus.Reason` is non-empty the projection appends ` (<reason>)` so operator surfaces preserve the explanation regardless of `State` value |
357	| `service.QuotaState.LastError` | Non-nil only when the harness method itself returned an error (call failure). State-driven absence (`State=QuotaUnavailable` etc.) does not populate `LastError`; it populates `Status`. |
358	| `service.AccountStatus.Authenticated` | `AccountSnapshot.Authenticated` |
359	| `service.AccountStatus.Unauthenticated` | `AccountSnapshot.Unauthenticated` |
360	| `service.AccountStatus.Email` | `AccountSnapshot.Email` |
361	| `service.AccountStatus.PlanType` | `AccountSnapshot.PlanType` |
362	| `service.AccountStatus.OrgName` | `AccountSnapshot.OrgName` |
363	| `service.AccountStatus.Source` | `AccountSnapshot.Source` |
364	| `service.AccountStatus.CapturedAt` | `AccountSnapshot.CapturedAt` |
365	| `service.AccountStatus.Fresh` | `AccountSnapshot.Fresh` |
366	| `service.AccountStatus.Detail` | `AccountSnapshot.Detail` |
367	| `service.HarnessInfo.Quota` | Result of `QuotaHarness.QuotaStatus()` projected via the rows above; nil when the harness does not implement `QuotaHarness` |
368	| `service.HarnessInfo.Account` | Result of `AccountHarness.AccountStatus()` projected; nil when the harness does not implement `AccountHarness` |
369	| `service.ProviderInfo.Quota` | Same projection as `HarnessInfo.Quota` for subscription-backed providers |
370	| `service.ProviderInfo.Auth` | Same projection as `HarnessInfo.Account` |
371	
372	Routing decisions inside the service consume `QuotaStatus.RoutingPreference`
373	directly. The service MUST NOT project `RoutingPreference` into the public
374	contract; it remains an internal routing signal.
375	
376	`HarnessInfo.Quota` and `HarnessInfo.Account` projections MUST remain
377	backwards-compatible in JSON shape with the current CONTRACT-003 schema.
378	Adding fields is allowed; removing or renaming existing public fields
379	requires a CONTRACT-003 amendment.

393	## Invariants
394	
395	These invariants are enforced by reviewer attention and (where practical)
396	by `go vet`-shaped tooling:
397	
398	1. **No service-side import of `internal/harnesses/<name>` symbols beyond
399	   `Runner{}` construction.** Permitted imports from outside the harness's
400	   own package and `internal/harnesses` itself: the runner constructor
401	   used by `internal/serviceimpl/execute_dispatch.go`. All other
402	   consumption MUST go through the interface methods on `Harness`,
403	   `QuotaHarness`, `AccountHarness`, or `ModelDiscoveryHarness`.
404	2. **Cache I/O is harness-owned.** No code outside
405	   `internal/harnesses/<name>/` reads or writes the harness's cache
406	   files.
407	3. **Concrete snapshot types are package-private.** The per-harness
408	   types that today are exported as `ClaudeQuotaSnapshot`,
409	   `CodexQuotaSnapshot`, `GeminiQuotaSnapshot`, etc., become lowercase
410	   (package-private). The interface contract returns `QuotaStatus`.
411	4. **Service routing reads only `RoutingPreference`, `State`, and
412	   `Windows`.** No service-side scoring rule may branch on `Detail`
413	   map contents or internal fields of the per-harness snapshot.
414	   `Windows` is the authoritative structured surface for tier or
415	   per-window facts.
416	5. **No cross-harness imports.** `claude` does not import `codex`;
417	   `claude-tui` (when introduced) does not import `claude`; etc. Shared
418	   helpers go in a neutral package (e.g.
419	   `internal/harnesses/anthropic/`).
420	6. **Runners are stateless wrappers around harness-owned cache files.**
421	   The `Runner` struct MAY hold immutable configuration (binary path,
422	   discovery cache pointer) and lock handles; it MUST NOT hold mutable
423	   quota or account state that would diverge across instances. Two
424	   `&Runner{}` instances of the same harness MUST observe identical
425	   `QuotaStatus`/`AccountSnapshot` results for the same cache state.
426	   The service MAY hold a single registered instance per harness or
427	   construct fresh instances per call; both patterns MUST produce
428	   equivalent observable behavior.
429	7. **`RefreshQuota` and `RefreshAccount` are single-flight per harness
430	   instance, mediated by the harness's on-disk cache lock (ADR-012).**
431	   Concurrent callers block on the lock; once the in-flight refresh
432	   completes, queued callers observe the new cached state. Probe
433	   failure surfaces in the returned status's `State` field, not as an
434	   error return.
435	8. **Errors are reserved for call failure.** `QuotaStatus`,
436	   `RefreshQuota`, `AccountStatus`, and `RefreshAccount` return an
437	   error ONLY for context cancellation, lock acquisition failure, or
438	   unrecoverable IO error. Absence of evidence, missing auth, blocked
439	   quota, and probe failures are reported as state on a valid
440	   returned value. This makes consumer code uniform across success and
441	   failure surfaces.

443	## Non-Goals
444	
445	- Refactoring CONTRACT-003 public types. Their shapes stay the same;
446	  only their *source* changes from per-harness exports to interface
447	  projection.
448	- Generalizing the `HarnessConfig` registry struct. Subprocess-specific
449	  fields (`BaseArgs`, `PermissionArgs`, `ModelFlag`) remain on the
450	  registry struct; they are configuration, not part of the interface.
451	- Introducing a plugin loader or out-of-tree harness support. Harnesses
452	  remain in-tree under `internal/harnesses/`.
453	- Promoting `claude-tui` to a primary harness identity. ADR-013 is
454	  withdrawn pending this contract; re-proposal is a follow-up spec.
455	
456	## Acceptance Criteria
457	
458	1. `internal/harnesses/types.go` declares `Harness`, `QuotaHarness`,
459	   `AccountHarness`, and `ModelDiscoveryHarness` interfaces with the
460	   signatures above.
461	2. `QuotaStatus`, `AccountSnapshot`, `QuotaStateValue`,
462	   `RoutingPreference`, and the three sentinel errors are declared in
463	   `internal/harnesses/types.go`.
464	3. Every existing harness implementation in `internal/harnesses/<name>/`
465	   satisfies `Harness` plus the documented optional sub-interfaces.
466	4. No `.go` file outside `internal/harnesses/` imports a symbol from
467	   `internal/harnesses/claude`, `internal/harnesses/codex`,
468	   `internal/harnesses/gemini`, `internal/harnesses/opencode`, or
469	   `internal/harnesses/pi` other than the runner constructor used by
470	   `internal/serviceimpl/execute_dispatch.go`. A linter check enforces
471	   this.
472	5. Public CONTRACT-003 JSON shapes for `HarnessInfo`, `ProviderInfo`,
473	   `QuotaState`, and `AccountStatus` are byte-identical (modulo
474	   intentionally added fields) to pre-refactor fixtures.
475	6. Per-harness `*QuotaSnapshot` types are lowercased (package-private).
476	7. Per-harness `*QuotaRoutingDecision` types are removed in favor of
477	   `QuotaStatus.RoutingPreference`.
478	8. Per-harness cache I/O functions (`Read*Quota`, `Write*Quota`,
479	   `*QuotaCachePath`) are unexported.
480	9. Conformance evidence (above) lands for every existing harness.
481	10. CONTRACT-003 cross-references CONTRACT-004 as the source for
482	    `HarnessInfo.Quota` and `HarnessInfo.Account` population.

8	# ADR-012: Per-Source On-Disk Cache for Discovery + Runtime Signals
9	
10	| Date | Status | Deciders | Related | Confidence |
11	|------|--------|----------|---------|------------|
12	| 2026-05-11 | Accepted | Fizeau maintainers | `ADR-009`, `ADR-010` | High |
13	
14	## Context
15	
16	The `fiz models` command (bead EPIC) must produce an available-models snapshot
17	that combines two tiers of information and feeds `route(client_inputs,
18	fiz_models_snapshot)`:
19	
20	- **Discovery signals** — whether a source exposes a model at all
21	  (provider `/v1/models` endpoint, harness PTY enumeration,
22	  `/props` introspection). Slow to collect: PTY enumeration takes
23	  ~30 s; OR `/api/v1/models` takes ~316 ms p50 over the open
24	  internet.
25	- **Runtime signals** — quota availability, rate-limit headroom,
26	  observed latency. Change frequently (5-min order) but don't affect
27	  model existence.
28	
29	Three requirements conflict without a cache:
30	
31	1. **UI latency ≤ 100 ms.** `fiz models` must return stale data immediately
32	   rather than block on discovery IO.
33	2. **Multi-process safety.** `ddx work`, `ddx try`, `fiz models`,
34	   and the routing layer all run concurrently and must share cache
35	   state without corruption or thundering-herd re-discovery.
36	3. **Crash safety.** A killed refresh process must not leave the cache in a
37	   corrupt or permanently-locked state.
38	
39	Fizeau has no required daemon. Its cache contract is cache-first reads plus
40	coordinated refresh through cross-process locks. `fiz models` and route hot
41	paths are quick by default: stale snapshot data is returned immediately when
42	freshness is pending. They may request a best-effort background refresh for
43	stale fields, but only through the same lock, marker, and single-flight path
44	used by blocking refresh; a short-lived CLI process must not spawn independent
45	probe storms or make correctness depend on a detached worker. `fiz models
46	--refresh` blocks on routing-relevant stale fields, and `fiz models
47	--refresh-all` blocks on every refreshable field. Without a long-running
48	freshness maintainer, stale output should tell the operator to run `fiz models
49	--refresh` or start/configure a DDx server freshness heartbeat.
50	
51	Fizeau already has a battle-tested file-locking idiom in
52	`cmd/bench/matrix.go:acquireMatrixLock` (lines 1222–1259): atomic
53	`O_CREATE|O_EXCL` create, JSON `{PID, StartedAt}` payload, crash
54	recovery via `syscall.Kill(pid, 0)`, cleanup-on-exit closure. The
55	harness quota caches (`internal/harnesses/claude/quota_cache.go`,
56	`internal/harnesses/codex/quota_cache.go`,
57	`internal/harnesses/gemini/quota_cache.go`) demonstrate the
58	atomic-write contract: write to `.tmp`, `os.Rename` to final path,
59	`chmod 0o600`.
60	
61	This ADR extends both idioms with a **two-tier lock + long-lived
62	refresh marker** pattern to handle the case where the IO under the
63	lock can take 30 s (PTY) — far longer than what a brief mutex is
64	designed to hold.
65	
66	## Decision
67	
68	### 1. File layout
69	
70	```
71	~/.cache/fizeau/              (os.UserCacheDir() + "/fizeau")
72	├── discovery/                # slow, stable; one file per source
73	│   ├── openrouter.json                 # 24 h TTL
74	│   ├── claude-subscription.json        # 24 h TTL
75	│   ├── codex-subscription.json         # 24 h TTL
76	│   ├── vidar-ds4.json                  # 1 h TTL  (LAN, local)
77	│   └── sindri-club-3090-llamacpp.json  # 1 h TTL  (LAN, local)
78	└── runtime/                  # hot, volatile; one file per source
79	    ├── openrouter.json                 # 5 min TTL
80	    ├── claude-subscription.json        # 5 min TTL
81	    └── ...
82	```
83	
84	Source names are kebab-case slugs derived from the provider entry in
85	fizeau's config (same identifier used by the routing layer). Each
86	data file is JSON. Top-level keys are fizeau's canonical model
87	identities: `<provider>/<model_id>` (e.g.
88	`openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4-5`). Alongside each data file,
89	the cache manager may write two side-car files:
90	
91	- `<source>.lock` — brief mutation lock (held for microseconds).
92	- `<source>.refreshing` — long-lived refresh marker (held for the
93	  duration of the IO, up to `RefreshDeadline`).
94	
95	### 2. TTL defaults
96	
97	All values are operator-configurable via environment variables or the
98	fizeau config file. The env-var names are the canonical override
99	mechanism; config-file keys mirror them.
100	
101	| Signal tier | Source type | Default TTL | Env override |
102	|-------------|-------------|-------------|--------------|
103	| Discovery | PTY enumeration | 24 h | `FIZ_TTL_DISCOVERY_PTY` |
104	| Discovery | HTTP `/v1/models` (remote) | 24 h | `FIZ_TTL_DISCOVERY_HTTP_REMOTE` |
105	| Discovery | HTTP `/v1/models` (LAN) | 1 h | `FIZ_TTL_DISCOVERY_HTTP_LOCAL` |
106	| Runtime | Any | 5 min | `FIZ_TTL_RUNTIME` |
107	
108	Lock and deadline constants:
109	
110	| Constant | Default | Env override |
111	|----------|---------|--------------|
112	| Lock acquisition timeout | 100 ms | `FIZ_LOCK_TIMEOUT` |
113	| Refresh deadline — PTY | 60 s | `FIZ_REFRESH_DEADLINE_PTY` |
114	| Refresh deadline — HTTP discovery | 10 s | `FIZ_REFRESH_DEADLINE_HTTP` |
115	| Refresh deadline — runtime | 5 s | `FIZ_REFRESH_DEADLINE_RUNTIME` |
116	| Marker staleness threshold | 2 × refresh deadline | derived |
117	
118	**Rationale:** PTY is the slowest path; 60 s is conservative but not
119	unreachable on a cold harness boot. HTTP remote (OR) is ~316 ms p50
120	measured; 10 s is a 30× headroom factor. LAN endpoints respond in
121	< 15 ms; the 1 h TTL trades off freshness against SSH-tunnel startup
122	cost. Runtime signals change on a ~5 min order (quota windows, rate-
123	limit headers), matching the TTL.
124	
125	### 3. Lock + marker pattern (two-tier)
126	
127	**Tier 1 — `<source>.lock`** (brief mutation lock):
128	
129	Identical to `acquireMatrixLock` semantics. Held only during state
130	transitions: "claim refresh slot" and "commit refresh result". Held
131	for microseconds. Uses `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` atomic create. Crash
132	recovery: if the owning PID is dead (`syscall.Kill(pid, 0)` returns
133	`ESRCH`), the lock is removed and the caller retries once.
134	
135	JSON payload: `{"pid": <int>, "started_at": "<RFC3339>"}`.
136	
137	**Tier 2 — `<source>.refreshing`** (long-lived refresh marker):
138	
139	Written after the lock is acquired and claimed. Held for the duration
140	of the IO. Other processes inspect this marker to decide whether to
141	wait or return stale data immediately. It is removed (under the Tier
142	1 lock) after the data file is atomically committed.
143	
144	JSON payload:
145	```json
146	{
147	  "pid": <int>,
148	  "started_at": "<RFC3339>",
149	  "deadline": "<RFC3339>"
150	}
151	```
152	
153	A marker is considered **stale** (orphan) when either:
154	- `now > deadline + staleness_threshold` (2 × refresh deadline), OR
155	- `syscall.Kill(pid, 0)` returns `ESRCH` (process dead).
156	
157	Stale markers are overridden by the next caller during `claim_refresh`
158	(the marker is removed under the Tier 1 lock before a new one is
159	written).
160	
161	### 4. Algorithms (pseudocode)
162	
163	#### Algorithm 1 — `claim_refresh(source) → ClaimedByMe | AlreadyInFlight(marker)`
164	
165	```
166	func claim_refresh(source):
167	    acquire tier-1 lock (timeout=LockAcquisitionTimeout):
168	        on timeout: return error "lock contention"
169	
170	    existing_marker = read_marker_if_exists(source)
171	
172	    if existing_marker != nil:
173	        if is_stale(existing_marker):
174	            remove(source.refreshing)   // orphan cleanup
175	        else:
176	            release tier-1 lock
177	            return AlreadyInFlight(existing_marker)
178	
179	    // Write the marker before releasing the lock so no other
180	    // process can claim the slot between lock release and marker
181	    // write.
182	    write_marker(source, pid=self, started_at=now,
183	                 deadline=now+RefreshDeadline(source))
184	    release tier-1 lock
185	    return ClaimedByMe
186	```
187	
188	#### Algorithm 2 — `refresh_and_commit(source)`
189	
190	```
191	func refresh_and_commit(source):
192	    claim = claim_refresh(source)
193	    if claim == AlreadyInFlight:
194	        return wait_for_refresh(source, claim.marker,
195	                                max_wait=RefreshDeadline(source))
196	
197	    // Perform slow IO outside any lock.
198	    data = fetch_source(source)   // PTY, HTTP, etc.
199	
200	    // Atomic commit (mirrors harness quota_cache.go pattern).
201	    tmp = source.data_path + ".tmp"
202	    write_json(tmp, data)
203	    chmod(tmp, 0o600)
204	    os.Rename(tmp, source.data_path)   // atomic on POSIX
205	
206	    // Remove marker under tier-1 lock.
207	    acquire tier-1 lock (timeout=LockAcquisitionTimeout):
208	        // Guard: if our deadline passed and another process
209	        // claimed the slot, do not remove the new marker.
210	        current_marker = read_marker_if_exists(source)
211	        if current_marker != nil && current_marker.pid == self:
212	            remove(source.refreshing)
213	    release tier-1 lock
214	```
215	
216	#### Algorithm 3 — `wait_for_refresh(source, marker, max_wait)`
217	
218	```
219	func wait_for_refresh(source, marker, max_wait):
220	    deadline = marker.deadline + staleness_threshold
221	    poll_interval = 250ms
222	    for now() < min(deadline, now() + max_wait):
223	        sleep(poll_interval)
224	        if not exists(source.refreshing):
225	            return read(source)   // refresh completed
226	        current = read_marker_if_exists(source)
227	        if current == nil:
228	            return read(source)   // refresh completed
229	        if is_stale(current):
230	            return read(source)   // orphan; return whatever is on disk
231	    // Timed out waiting; return stale data without error.
232	    return read(source)
233	```
234	
235	#### Algorithm 4 — `read(source) → (data, fresh_bool)`
236	
237	```
238	func read(source):
239	    if not exists(source.data_path):
240	        return (nil, false)
241	    data = read_json(source.data_path)   // no lock; file is immutable
242	                                          // until atomic rename
243	    fresh = (now() - data.captured_at) < TTL(source)
244	    return (data, fresh)
245	
246	    // NB: stale data is always returned without error. The caller
247	    // decides whether to trigger a background refresh.
248	    // Torn reads are impossible: rename is atomic on POSIX; a
249	    // reader either sees the old complete file or the new complete
250	    // file, never a partial write.
251	```
252	
253	#### Algorithm 5 — `force_refresh(source)`
254	
255	```
256	func force_refresh(source):
257	    // Synchronous. Bypasses TTL check. Waits for any in-flight
258	    // refresh to finish, then reads fresh data.
259	    claim = claim_refresh(source)
260	    if claim == AlreadyInFlight:
261	        wait_for_refresh(source, claim.marker,
262	                         max_wait=RefreshDeadline(source))
263	        data, _ = read(source)
264	        return data
265	
266	    // We hold the claim; run refresh synchronously.
267	    refresh_and_commit(source)
268	    data, _ = read(source)
269	    return data
270	```
271	
272	#### Algorithm 6 — In-process single-flight composition
273	
274	```
275	// singleflightGroup is a golang.org/x/sync/singleflight.Group,
276	// one per cache instance (process-lifetime).
277	//
278	// This composes with file-based coordination: within a process,
279	// singleflight ensures at most one goroutine runs refresh_and_commit
280	// per source. Across processes, the file-based marker (Algorithm 1)
281	// provides the same guarantee.
282	
283	func maybe_background_refresh(source):
284	    data, fresh = read(source)
285	    if fresh:
286	        return data
287	    // Stale or missing — request a best-effort refresh via
288	    // singleflight so concurrent callers share one goroutine.
289	    // Route hot paths also use this nonblocking form before scoring;
290	    // explicit refresh/preflight surfaces use ensure_fresh / force_refresh.
291	    go singleflightGroup.Do(source.key(), func():
292	        refresh_and_commit(source)
293	    )
294	    return data   // return stale immediately; never block UI
295	
296	func ensure_fresh(source):
297	    // Blocking variant used by force_refresh and tests.
298	    _, _, _ = singleflightGroup.Do(source.key(), func():
299	        refresh_and_commit(source)
300	    )
301	    data, _ = read(source)
302	    return data
303	```
304	
305	`singleflight.Group` deduplicates concurrent `Do` calls with the
306	same key: if a refresh is already running, a second caller blocks
307	on the same goroutine and gets the same result. This eliminates
308	the in-process thundering herd without file IO overhead.
309	
310	The background helper is optional and process-lifetime scoped. A `fiz models`
311	CLI invocation may call it after returning stale output, but no design depends
312	on the goroutine surviving after process exit. Long-running clients such as the
313	DDx server should call the same refresh APIs on a heartbeat when they want to
314	maintain fresh cache state asynchronously.
315	
316	### 5. Crash recovery
317	
318	No manual cleanup is required. Recovery happens lazily on the next
319	call to `claim_refresh`:
320	
321	- **Stale `.lock` file** (dead PID): removed on next acquisition
322	  attempt, same as `acquireMatrixLock` semantics.
323	- **Stale `.refreshing` marker** (dead PID or past deadline +
324	  staleness threshold): removed under tier-1 lock before a new
325	  marker is written.
326	- **Partial data write** (`.tmp` file left behind): safe to remove
327	  or overwrite on the next `refresh_and_commit`; the final
328	  `os.Rename` was never called so the committed data file is
329	  intact.
330	
331	### 6. Force-refresh semantics
332	
333	`force_refresh` is synchronous and bypasses the TTL check. It:
334	
335	1. Inspects the marker. If a refresh is already in flight, waits
336	   up to `RefreshDeadline` for it to complete.
337	2. If no refresh is in flight, runs one synchronously.
338	3. Returns fresh data.
339	
340	Used by `fiz models --refresh`, by the `fiz cache refresh <source>`
341	subcommand, and by explicit preflight/test surfaces. `ResolveRoute` and
342	`Execute` do not use this blocking path for ordinary autorouting: they read
343	cached facts immediately, request coordinated background refresh for stale or
344	missing local/provider facts, and let cached failure evidence gate known-dead
345	providers.
346	
347	`--refresh-all` is the strict variant that blocks until all refreshable fields
348	are fresh enough for display, not just the routing-relevant subset. It uses the
349	same refresh coordinator and marker discipline; it just widens the blocking
350	surface before returning snapshot data.
351	
352	### 7. Cache prune
353	
354	`fiz cache prune` removes discovery and runtime data files (and
355	their sidecar lock/marker files) for sources not named in the
356	current fizeau config. The command is **explicit only** — it is
357	not called at startup. Rationale: auto-prune at startup could
358	silently discard a cache that another process is actively using;
359	the operator should decide when pruning is safe.
360	
361	Safety: `fiz cache prune` acquires the tier-1 lock for each source
362	before removing its files. It skips sources that have an active
363	`.refreshing` marker.
364	
365	### 8. Prior art: acquireMatrixLock extension
366	
367	`cmd/bench/matrix.go:acquireMatrixLock` (lines 1222–1259) is the
368	direct prior art for the tier-1 `.lock` file:
369	
370	- `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` atomic create.
371	- JSON `{PID, StartedAt}` payload for post-mortem inspection.
372	- `processAlive(PID)` (`syscall.Kill(pid, 0)`) for crash recovery.
373	- Single-use: acquired before a matrix cell run, released on exit.
374	
375	This ADR extends that pattern with a **separate** tier-2
376	`.refreshing` marker so that the tier-1 lock can be released
377	promptly after writing the marker. This is necessary because the
378	IO under the marker (PTY enumeration, HTTP) can take 30–60 s — far
379	longer than what a blocking lock should hold. The two-tier design
380	keeps the brief-lock semantics of `acquireMatrixLock` intact while
381	allowing other processes to observe in-progress refresh state.
382	
383	### 9. Mandatory test matrix for bead M1
384	
385	The implementation bead (M1) **must** ship all 10 tests passing.
386	No test may be skipped, marked as flaky, or guarded by a build tag.
387	Multi-process tests must use the standard `TestMain` +
388	`os.Args[0]` helper-process pattern (spawn the test binary itself
389	as a child process) to avoid requiring external binaries.
390	
391	| # | Name | What it proves |
392	|---|------|----------------|
393	| 1 | `TestConcurrentClaimTwoProcs` | Two child processes race `claim_refresh`; exactly one returns `ClaimedByMe`, the other `AlreadyInFlight`. |
394	| 2 | `TestReaderDuringRefresh` | Atomic rename guarantees no torn read: 100 concurrent readers observe only complete, checksummed versions while a writer produces 100 versions sequentially. |
395	| 3 | `TestCrashDuringRefresh` | A child process writes a marker and is killed (`SIGKILL`). Next process detects dead PID in marker and claims successfully. |
396	| 4 | `TestRefreshTimeout` | Marker deadline is set to `now - 1 s` (expired). Next process claims the slot; the original process's late commit is rejected (tier-1 lock check guards the marker removal). |
397	| 5 | `TestForceRefreshWaitsAndReadsFresh` | `force_refresh` with an in-flight marker waits until the refresh completes and returns the newly written data, not stale data. |
398	| 6 | `TestConcurrentNormalAndForce` | Concurrent `read` (normal) + `force_refresh`: normal returns stale immediately without blocking; `force_refresh` waits and singleflight deduplicates the goroutines. |
399	| 7 | `TestAtomicRenameVerified` | 100 concurrent readers + 1 writer producing 100 versions; every read returns a complete, consistent version (verified by checksum); no version is ever partially written. |
400	| 8 | `TestPruneDoesNotRaceActiveSources` | `fiz cache prune` with a source whose `.refreshing` marker is active; prune skips that source and does not remove any of its files. |
401	| 9 | `TestStaleWhileRevalidate` | Stale cache entry: `read` returns stale data immediately (≤ 5 ms); an optional background refresh request is coalesced through singleflight/markers; after a refresh completes, subsequent `read` returns fresh data. |
402	| 10 | `TestPIDReuseSafety` | Marker contains a PID that has since been reused by an unrelated OS process (alive check passes); deadline check is the safety net — marker is treated as stale once `now > deadline + staleness_threshold`. |
403	
404	## Consequences
405	
406	**Positive:**
407	
408	- `fiz models` does not hang by default. The read path is always cache-bounded
409	  (≤ 100 ms) because `read` never waits on IO — it returns stale
410	  data immediately and may request a coordinated best-effort background
411	  refresh.
412	- Autorouting remains responsive even when no DDx server or other long-running
413	  maintainer is active: route-time refresh requests use the same coordinated
414	  cache machinery in the background, while scoring consumes cached evidence.
415	- Multi-process safe across `ddx work`, `ddx try`, `fiz models`,
416	  and the routing layer. Exactly one process refreshes each source
417	  at a time; others either wait (force) or return stale
418	  (normal read).
419	- Crash-safe by construction. PID-alive checks and deadline
420	  checks together recover from all observed failure modes
421	  (kill -9, OOM, timeout).
422	- Reuses `acquireMatrixLock`'s proven `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` + PID
423	  idiom. No new cross-platform lock library is required.
424	- Each source has an independent lifecycle. OR re-discovery does
425	  not block PTY discovery. A slow PTY source does not delay the
426	  `fiz models` response for cloud sources.
427	- Atomic-rename write contract (from harness quota caches) ensures
428	  readers never observe a partial write.
429	
430	**Negative:**
431	
432	- Two sidecar files per source (`.lock` + `.refreshing`) is more
433	  structural complexity than a single in-process mutex.
434	- File-based coordination has inherent edge cases on network
435	  filesystems (NFS, CIFS) where `O_EXCL` and `rename` may not be
436	  atomic. The cache directory is always under `os.UserCacheDir()`,
437	  which is local on all supported platforms; NFS is not a target.
438	- PID reuse is a real (if rare) edge case: a new OS process that
439	  happens to get the same PID as the crashed refresher would
440	  defeat the PID-alive check. The deadline check is the safety
441	  net; the worst outcome is serving stale data past the deadline,
442	  which is within the acceptable degradation envelope.
443	- The test matrix (10 tests, several multi-process) is non-trivial
444	  to maintain. The `TestMain` helper-process pattern requires
445	  discipline: new multi-process tests must follow the established
446	  pattern or they will not work in CI.
447	
448	## Out of scope
449	
450	- Persistent storage of historical signals. The cache is
451	  current-state only; evicted entries are gone.
452	- Multi-machine cache sharing. Per-host only; distributed caches
453	  require coordination primitives beyond file locks.
454	- Compression. Files are plain JSON; the largest anticipated cache
455	  file (OR full model list) is ~200 KB uncompressed.
456	- Encryption at rest. Cache files contain no secrets; model lists
457	  and quota windows are non-sensitive operational data.
458	- OR sub-provider cache (deferred to bead M5). Sub-provider
459	  routing metadata warrants a separate cache tier with its own TTL
460	  strategy.
461	- NFS / network filesystem support. The cache directory is always
462	  local.
463	- A Fizeau-owned daemon. Asynchronous freshness is provided by callers that
464	  choose to run long-lived processes, such as a DDx server heartbeat, over the
465	  same synchronous lock-coordinated refresh primitives.
466

89	>
90	> ### Design direction for re-proposal
91	>
92	> The following decisions are recorded here so the future ADR-013
93	> re-proposer can adopt them without re-deriving the rationale. They
94	> are constraints, not interface contract — CONTRACT-004 and ADR-014
95	> remain unaffected and transport-agnostic.
96	>
97	> 1. **Transport**: in-process PTY via the existing `internal/pty/`
98	>    library, with hooks registered via `--settings '<inline-json>'`
99	>    (Anthropic-published extension point). The `--settings` flag is
100	>    explicitly distinguished from the previously-forbidden batch flags
101	>    (`--print`, `-p`, `--output-format`, `--stream-json`, `--effort`,
102	>    `--model`, `--permission-mode`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`)
103	>    because it configures end-user-facing behavior the way a user's
104	>    `~/.claude/settings.json` would, not an automation/batch mode. The
105	>    batch-flag prohibition stands; the `--settings` carve-out is
106	>    additive.
107	>
108	> 2. **Output parsing**: read the JSONL transcript whose path is
109	>    delivered in the `Stop` hook payload. Do not parse rendered TUI
110	>    output. `internal/pty/terminal` (vt10x) is not required for
111	>    Execute; the PTY layer is reduced to "enough to keep Ink happy at
112	>    startup" — a small responder for DA1 / DA2 / DSR / XTVERSION /
113	>    window-size probes. A reusable startup-probe responder belongs in
114	>    `internal/pty/` so the quota probe path can consume it too.
115	>
116	> 3. **Streaming progress events**: use `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse`
117	>    hooks (or whichever Claude Code hooks are documented for tool-call
118	>    boundaries at re-proposal time) to emit `tool_call` / `tool_result`
119	>    events during the turn. claude-p is batch (only `Stop`); Fizeau's
120	>    CONTRACT-004 requires intermediate `ProgressEvents` so this hook
121	>    set is load-bearing.
122	>
123	> 4. **Session lifetime**: **pooled long-lived sessions with `/clear`
124	>    between turns, lifetime bounded by the fiz process**. Rationale:
125	>    Ink + auth startup is the expensive part (~50–200 ms per claude-p's
126	>    measurements); amortizing it across the many Execute calls within
127	>    a single fiz invocation is worth the pool-management cost.
128	>    `/clear` resets conversation state without dropping the warm
129	>    session. The pool dies when fiz dies — no PID files, no daemon, no
130	>    cross-invocation persistence.
131	>
132	>    Pool key default: **per `(harness, workdir)`**. Claude sessions
133	>    are bound to a working directory at startup; switching workdirs in
134	>    an existing session is not supported by `claude`. Per-(harness)
135	>    only would force serialization across all workdirs;
136	>    per-(harness, workdir, model) is overkill — model selection is
137	>    cheap enough to run via `/model` post-`/clear`.
138	>
139	>    Pool depth default: **1 per key**. Adequate for serial agent
140	>    loops, which is the standalone CLI's usage. Service-mode
141	>    concurrency can raise this with no contract change.
142	>
143	>    Pool placement: the pool lives at package scope (a singleton in
144	>    `internal/harnesses/claude-tui/`) or at service scope (a
145	>    constructor-injected dependency on the Runner), **not as a field
146	>    on the Runner struct**. Two `&claudetui.Runner{}` instances must
147	>    share the pool, otherwise the dispatcher's "construct a fresh
148	>    Runner per Execute" pattern defeats the amortization. CONTRACT-004
149	>    invariant #6 forbids mutable quota/account state on the Runner
150	>    but does not forbid shared transport state behind a singleton;
151	>    this is the right escape valve.
152	>
153	> 5. **Empirical `/clear` semantics gate** (pre-implementation): verify
154	>    against the installed Claude Code that `/clear`:
155	>    - resets conversation history (the point of the command);
156	>    - does NOT reset model selection (otherwise per-turn `/model` is
157	>      required, lengthening the per-turn ritual);
158	>    - does NOT reset permission mode;
159	>    - does NOT close the auth/session token;
160	>    - starts a new transcript file at a path observable from the
161	>      next turn's `Stop` hook payload.
162	>
163	>    If any of those don't hold, the per-turn ritual lengthens but
164	>    the pool model is still worthwhile. If `/clear` doesn't exist or
165	>    is unstable in the installed version, fall back to per-Execute
166	>    sessions (claude-p model) and accept the cold-start cost.
167	>
168	> 6. **Orphan reaper**: fiz crashes leave pooled `claude` processes
169	>    orphaned. A startup reaper analogous to the existing
170	>    `service_stale_harness_reaper*.go` kills `claude` processes whose
171	>    parent fiz PID is gone, before the new fiz instance constructs
172	>    its pool. No persistent state across fiz invocations — the
173	>    reaper inspects live process state only.
174	>
175	> 7. **Hook conflict handling**: a user's existing
176	>    `~/.claude/settings.json` may declare its own `SessionStart` /
177	>    `Stop` / `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` hooks. The `--settings
178	>    '<inline-json>'` mechanism's merge semantics (replace vs. layer)
179	>    are unspecified in claude-p's README and need explicit
180	>    verification before claude-tui can ship. If hooks are
181	>    replace-not-merge, Fizeau must compose with whatever the operator
182	>    already has, not stomp it.
183	>
184	> 8. **Subscription billing observation**: still required as a
185	>    promotion gate per ADR-014. Neither claude-p nor shannon claims
186	>    subscription billing; both route through the same `claude`
187	>    binary and inherit whatever billing classification that binary's
188	>    request paths produce. The re-proposal must include an empirical
189	>    measurement showing PTY+hooks-driven Claude moves the `/usage`
190	>    window, otherwise the fork's economic premise is unverified.
